boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Chusto-Talasah (Caving Banks) record (December 9, 1861) in Operations in the Indian Territory [November-December 1861]. The December 8 dispersal of Drew's Cherokee regiment and Cooper's withdrawal to Fort Gibson are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field has no figures; the live field reads CS 1,300 and the description Cooper's 1,300. Cooper started with 780 and ordered Drew's detachment of about 500 and Sims's Texans to join him; Drew's regiment dispersed in panic the night before the battle. He says his force actually engaged did not exceed 1,100, and that the enemy was certainly over 2,500, 4,000 by Cherokee prisoners, after an escaped prisoner's report of 2,000; at the house his men never equalled half the enemy's. Britton gives Cooper some eleven hundred mounted men with Drew's five hundred and Sims's three hundred.
claims.rationale: Column, engaged and estimated opposing figures of different moments; the CWSAC 1,300 is not traced. No account by Opothleyahola's side was inspected; every figure for his force and losses is an opponent's estimate or a history's. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel Douglas H. Cooper and Opothleyahola; the live page gives Cooper as Brigadier General. Cooper formed three columns and ordered D. N. McIntosh's Creek regiment to turn the enemy's right. Britton credits the chief with choosing the position.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report and a history; the live rank is not adopted and there is no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory; NPS says Cooper drove the defenders across Bird Creek. Cooper says the enemy disappeared from his front after over four hours; Britton says the Confederates withdrew to their camp five miles back and Cooper, badly crippled, retreated to Fort Gibson.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 464 (US 412; CS 52). Cooper reports 15 killed and 37 wounded and says prisoners admitted an enemy loss of 412, probably 500; Britton repeats Cooper's figures but says the chief's loss, though not known, was much less than the Confederates'.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The live US 412 equals the prisoners' figure in Cooper's report; that is not independent confirmation.

open_questions: D. N. McIntosh's, Drew's, Sims's, Hall's, McCurtain's and Pitchlynn's reports (Nos. 4-9), returns and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cooper's January 20, 1862 report covers all three engagements and is an interested Confederate account; it is written after McIntosh's January 1 report and criticizes McIntosh. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, vol. I (second edition, 1891) is a retrospective history by a Union soldier of the border army, based by its title page on the official reports; it is not independent of the report families. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
